stdout_tail:
Both `analysis.py` and `result.json` are saved in the working directory.

**Finding:** The model (HistGradientBoostingClassifier) is well-calibrated. On a held-out 40% test split, the Expected Calibration Error is 0.0073, Max Calibration Error is 0.0336, Brier score is 0.0877, and a calibration-curve regression gives slope ≈1.03 / intercept ≈0.016 (ideal: slope=1, intercept=0) — predicted probabilities track observed outcome frequencies closely across all 10 probability bins, with only mild overconfidence in the 0.4–0.5 and 0.8–0.9 bins. A logistic regression baseline showed comparably good calibration (ECE 0.0063), reinforcing the conclusion.

parsed_result.summary: A HistGradientBoostingClassifier trained on the Adult Income data is reasonably well-calibrated: its Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on a held-out test set is 0.0073 (Brier score 0.0877), with predicted probabilities tracking observed outcome frequencies closely across probability bins, though the model is very slightly overconfident. A plain logistic regression baseline is similarly well-calibrated by construction (ECE 0.0063).
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Expected Calibration Error (ECE, 10 equal-width bins, GBM test set)
parsed_result.direction: model is well-calibrated (low ECE, near-diagonal reliability curve)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Model: HistGradientBoostingClassifier (primary) plus LogisticRegression (comparison), both from scikit-learn with default-ish hyperparameters (GBM: max_iter=200). Preprocessing: rows with '?' treated as missing; numeric features standard-scaled; categorical features one-hot encoded (unknown categories ignored at test time). Target: binary, '>50K'=1. Validation: single stratified 60/40 train/test split (random_state=42), no cross-validation or post-hoc recalibration (e.g. Platt scaling or isotonic regression) applied — calibration assessed on raw predict_proba output. Calibration metrics: 10 equal-width probability bins for reliability diagram, Expected Calibration Error (sample-weighted mean |confidence-accuracy| across bins), Maximum Calibration Error, Brier score, and logistic calibration slope/intercept (regressing outcome on logit of predicted probability) as a complementary check. No class-imbalance correction (e.g. class_weight='balanced') was applied, since calibration should be judged on the model's natural predicted probabilities.
